text:
simon: Heads-up — experiment idea: opt-in shim that routes clients without X-Redwood-Version to v1, but if they opt-in via header we route to v2. Keep telemetry to measure surprise failures.
anya: Sounds reasonable. How do we surface opt-in in console?
devon: We could add a per-tenant toggle under API > Compatibility. Default off. When enabled, console adds a short-lived cookie/flag and we accept X-Redwood-Optin: clockwork header for routing.
lina: We need to be careful with quotas: v2 token accounting differs (batching + prefix caching). If a tenant toggles, we should show estimated delta in cost preview.
simon: Agreed. Also thinking: server-side fallback if v2 capacity constrained -> fall back to v1 with a header in response: X-Redwood-Fallback: v1. That way clients can detect and degrade gracefully.
anya: Make sure we emit telemetry events: route.handshake.request, route.handshake.fallback, and route.handshake.latency. Sample rate 1% by default, 100% for tenants that opt-in so we get richer signals.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for "compat-shim-clockwork" in eng-platform tomorrow 08:00 UTC.
devon: On the API surface: propose header names: X-Redwood-Version: v1|v2 and X-Redwood-Optin: clockwork=true. If both present and conflict, prefer explicit Version header.
lina: For billing preview: add a modal that shows per-hour token rate delta and worst-case 95th percentile latency change. We can compute using recent workload histograms.
simon: Edge-case: persistent sticky routing — if a request uses v2 and writes state to KV-cache or external store, then a subsequent v1 request may not find it. Need to document caveat and provide a migration flag: 'session_migrate=true' to force affinity to v2 for same token for 24h.
anya: UX: console should show a red banner when any tenant has opted-in but we detect >0.5% fallback rate to v1 for that tenant. Link to rollbacks and quick disable.
devon: Implementation notes: middleware to check headers, consult tenant flag store (fast memcache), then apply routing decision. Emit decision.trace id. Pseudocode: 
```
route = (header.Version) ? header.Version : (tenant.optin ? 'v2' : 'v1')
if (route == 'v2' && capacity.low) { emit('route.handshake.fallback'); route='v1' }
```

lina: Telemetry schema: include fields: tenant_id, route_chosen, fallback_reason, sampled_trace_id. Add mapping to billing pipeline.
simon: Action items: 1) devon to add header parsing + fallback hook (PR request). 2) lina to prototype billing delta preview. 3) anya to mock console toggle + banner copy. 4) ops to schedule canary.
ops-bot: reminder: please add feature flag "compat_clockwork_shim" in flags-service before PR merge.
anya: I'll draft console copy: "Opt in to v2 routing for this tenant. v2 may change latency/cost. We will show fallback events in the dashboard."
devon: I'll open the PR with unit tests for header precedence and a small integration test for fallback path.
lina: I'll add a sampling job to ensure telemetry joins billing ids so we can compute cost delta per tenant.
simon: If fallback spikes during canary, we auto-disable the opt-in for affected tenants and notify owners. We'll copy that into runbook.
anya: ok — I'll create the canary checklist and link runbook.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary scheduled. watchers: @simon @anya @devon @lina
simon: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the coordination log.
